title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is not part of the 1976 divided-power De Rham notes. It is a typed page, p. 67 of Exposé IX, from SGA 7 I: Grothendieck, 'Modèles de Néron et monodromie', 1967–69, published in LNM 288 (1972). It has been filed in cote 136 between handwritten pages about the simplicial divided-power algebras A_•(S,S^+,t).

First paragraph: end of the proof of 5.9, an extension property for morphisms into Néron models. The last hypothesis reduces to the case G' = A and u = id. Then v_η : G_η → A_η is a projection to be extended to v : G → A. G is smooth, being an extension of two smooth group schemes. So the Néron mapping property of A (it extends K-morphisms from smooth S-schemes) gives the extension.

Corollary 5.10: Let S be a trait (DVR spectrum) with fraction field K, A_K an abelian variety over K, and ℓ a prime. When ℓ = p (the residue characteristic), assume char K = 0 so Tate's full-faithfulness theorem for p-divisible groups (used in 5.8) applies. Then A_K has good reduction iff its ℓ-divisible (Barsotti–Tate) group extends to a Barsotti–Tate group over S. This is the conjecture stated in Grothendieck's ICM Nice 1970 talk ([8, 4.9]).

Proof as far as this page goes:
- Necessity is clear.
- The case ℓ ≠ p is Néron–Ogg–Shafarevich, already done in 2.2.9.
- Reduce to S henselian.
- Semi-stable case: 5.8 with F = X gives T_ℓ(A_K) = T_ℓ(A_K)^f, i.e. the whole ℓ-divisible group is 'finite'. Hence the toric part of the special fibre A_0 is zero, so A_0^0 is an abelian variety and A has good reduction (2.2.9(iii)).
- General case: reduce to S strictly local. Choose a finite Galois K'/K over which A has semi-stable reduction (3.6). Let A* be the Néron model over the normalisation S'. G = Gal(K'/K) acts on (A*, S'). The proof continues on the next typescript page, presumably by showing the inertia action on the special fibre is trivial, hence good reduction over S.
errors: Typo in the typescript: 'Soir K'' should be 'Soit K''.
No mathematical errors. The ℓ = p case depends on Tate's theorem (char K = 0), as stated.

ideas.what: Néron mapping property used to extend a projection G_η → A_η from a smooth group extension G
Good reduction criterion via extension of the p-divisible group (char 0, ℓ = p), proved using Tate's theorem and semistable reduction
ideas.modern_name: p-adic Néron–Ogg–Shafarevich criterion via Barsotti–Tate groups (Grothendieck's criterion)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck, SGA 7 IX Cor. 5.10 (conjectured at ICM 1970)
ideas.where_published: SGA 7 I (LNM 288), Exp. IX, Cor. 5.10; conjecture in 'Groupes de Barsotti-Tate et cristaux', ICM Nice 1970, 4.9

ideas.what: Semi-stable case: finite part equals whole Tate module, so toric part vanishes, so good reduction
ideas.modern_name: Grothendieck's orthogonality / finite-part theorem for semi-abelian reduction

deep.surprise_reason: This is a typed page of the published SGA 7 Exposé IX, containing the well-known Corollary 5.10. It is misfiled among the 1976 divided-power De Rham notes and has no connection to the neighbouring handwritten pages. Its only interest is archival: a typescript page of SGA 7 sits in this folder.
transcription_corrections: The page is a typescript of SGA 7 Exp. IX p. 67 (stamped 385), not handwritten notes.
'Soir K'' is a typo in the original for 'Soit K''.
'A_o' denotes the special fibre A_0 of the Néron model and 'A_o^o' its identity component; 'iii^o' is likely 'iii)'.
